common: Match the art style of the reference image exactly: a hand-made cut-paper collage, like a 1950s children's picture book made from coloured paper. Every shape is a flat piece of cut or torn coloured paper with a subtle paper grain and slightly irregular hand-cut edges, simple drawn lines for stone courses, roof slates and planks, tiny soft shadows where paper layers overlap, and a limited warm palette of honey stone, cream, sage and olive greens, duck-egg blue sky, mustard, tomato red and teal. Soft, even spring morning light. Eye-level viewpoint with the buildings, front doors and windows large and clearly visible across the middle of the picture, doors and window frames as clean, bold, separate pieces of paper. The foreground ground (paths, lawn, cobbles or flagstones) runs across the full width along the bottom third of the picture, made of a few large calm pieces of paper with only faint joints, so small objects lying on it are easy to see. A strip of sky with paper clouds along the top, kept fairly plain. No people, no vehicles, no text, no lettering, no numbers, no litter. Very wide 2:1 panorama, full-bleed illustration edge to edge, no border, no frame.

plates.railway-halt: Scene: a tiny country railway halt in the Cotswolds, seen from the platform. The long flagstone platform with a pale painted edge runs across the whole foreground. On the left, the honey-stone station building with a tall chimney and a panelled front door; in the middle, a wooden waiting shelter with a scalloped valance canopy in chocolate brown and cream; two tall cast-iron platform gas lamps, a wooden platform bench, flower beds and a white picket fence along the back of the platform. On the right, the single railway line curves away past a semaphore signal into rolling green hills dotted with sheep. Blossom trees.
plates.high-street: Scene: the high street of a Cotswold village, looking along the gently rising lane which curves away in the centre of the picture. Honey-stone cottages and little shops with steep stone-slate roofs and tall chimneys line both sides: on the left a post office with a bow window and empty iron sign brackets; on the right a tea room with a striped awning, a red telephone kiosk and a red pillar box; front doors in different colours, white sash windows, black iron street lamps. A wide cobbled lane and flagstone pavements fill the foreground. A church tower and hills in the distance.

village-green.prompt: Scene: a close, intimate corner of the village green at Honeycombe, seen at eye level from the lawn, as if standing a few steps away. On the left, the old stone Market Cross stands large and clear: a tall carved honey-stone shaft topped with a small stone cross, on a wide stepped octagonal base of three steps; the whole cross fits inside the picture with a little sky above it. In the middle, a flagstone path crosses the lawn to one long wooden park bench with a slatted back, set in front of a low clipped hedge and a flower border. On the right, the stone-edged kerb of the duck pond with clear blue water, reeds, yellow flag irises and three mallard ducks, and a weeping willow trailing over the far bank. Behind the hedge, the fronts of two or three honey-stone cottages with coloured front doors, and the church tower small in the distance; only a narrow strip of sky with a couple of paper clouds along the top. The lawn in the foreground is a few large calm pieces of fresh green paper, with clear empty grass to the left of the bench, in front of the bench and between the path and the pond. Only one bench. No noticeboard, no flower tubs, no bins, no deckchairs, no bird bath, no duck house, no people, no text.
village-green.note: Close work area for the Green (visual playtest 2026-09-27). The earlier wide view is kept in plates_wide/.

plates.weavers-row: Scene: a row of steep-roofed seventeenth-century weavers' cottages in honey stone stepping along the left and middle of the picture, with dormer windows, mullioned casements and brightly painted front doors, beside a clear shallow river that runs across the right side and foreground. A small arched stone footbridge over the river, a wall lantern, a grassy riverbank and a gravel footpath. Ducks on the water, a weeping willow on the right, reeds and water meadows.
plates.old-mill: Scene: an old three-storey honey-stone watermill with a big wooden waterwheel on the left, a shallow ford where a country lane splashes through a stream across the foreground, stepping stones, a low arched stone packhorse bridge on the right, a mill cottage with a stable door, a lantern by the mill door, a wooden sluice gate. Trees and hills beyond.
plates.bee-and-bramble: Scene: a cosy thatched country pub with honey-stone walls filling the right two thirds of the picture: a rose-covered timber porch around an oak front door, small leaded windows, a pair of carriage lanterns, an empty iron sign bracket on the wall. On the left a low dry-stone wall with a wooden garden gate, a hawthorn hedge and rolling hills. Wooden picnic tables and benches on a gravel forecourt and a lawn in the foreground.
plates.st-aldhelms: Scene: a honey-stone Cotswold parish church on the right with a square crenellated tower bearing a round blue-and-gold clock face, an arched oak church door in a stone porch, tall arched windows. On the left, a wooden lychgate with a stone-tiled roof and an open gate, a cast-iron lamp post, a dry-stone wall. A flagstone path leads from the lychgate past two clipped yew trees and a few weathered headstones among daffodils and primroses; a wooden parish noticeboard. Path and grass in the foreground.
plates.rose-cottage: Scene: a thatched honey-stone cottage on the right with a green front door under a rose-covered porch, a lantern by the door, small casement windows and hollyhocks. On the left a cottage garden: three white wooden beehives, a little wooden greenhouse, a vegetable patch with bean poles, a washing line between posts, a scarecrow-free lawn, a wooden gate in a picket fence. A brick path winds through the lawn in the foreground; a garden bench.

village-shop.prompt: Texture matters most: the whole interior is built from cut and torn paper exactly like the reference pictures, with visible paper grain and fibres, slightly wobbly hand-cut edges and layered paper pieces with tiny soft shadows, the same texture density as the outdoor scene in the first reference; nothing smooth, glossy or computer-drawn. Scene: inside the village Post Office and General Stores in 1957, seen at eye level from just inside the door. On the left, a big multi-paned shop bow window with a deep wooden window sill inside, looking out onto a sunny honey-stone street with cottages opposite. Across the middle and right, a long dark wooden shop counter with a plain flat painted front panel in soft green, and on top of the counter a glass-fronted display case holding big jars of coloured boiled sweets, a brass till and brass weighing scales. Behind the counter, tall wooden shelves with tins, packets and jars shown as big simple blocks of colour, and at the back right a small Post Office counter with a brass grille. Cream and sage painted walls, a pendant lamp, a wooden floor of broad honey-coloured planks across the whole bottom third of the picture, calm and clear. Warm, welcoming daylight from the window. Leave clear empty floor in the foreground, empty space on the inside window sill and on the left-hand end of the counter. No people, no text, no lettering, no numbers, no price tickets, no signs.
village-shop.note: The shop interior (visual playtest 2026-09-27): Mrs Pemberton's Post Office & Stores on the High Street.
village-shop.restyle: Redraw the first reference image, keeping its composition exactly: the same bow window on the left with the honey-stone street outside, the same doorway, the same counter with its soft green panelled front, the same glass sweet case, brass till and scales, the same shelves of tins and jars, the same Post Office grille, pendant lamp and wide plank floor, all in the same places and at the same sizes. Rebuild everything in the cut-paper collage technique of the second and third reference images: every surface is a flat piece of cut or torn coloured paper or felt with visible paper grain and fibres, slightly wobbly hand-cut edges, simple drawn lines for planks and panels, and tiny soft shadows where the paper layers overlap. Walls and floor show the paper texture clearly; nothing smooth, glossy or computer-drawn. Colours of a fresh spring day, as in the references: warm honey planks, cream walls, soft sage-green paintwork, clear blue sky outside, bright jars. No people, no text, no lettering, no numbers. Very wide 2:1 panorama, full-bleed, no border.
